# The share of a class's PIT mutants that its @ConcurrencyTestFor test detects on its own.
#
# .github/scripts/concurrency_test_kills.py runs PIT once per marker pair, with the named class
# (and its nested classes) as the only target and the marked test as the only test, and fails the
# weekly mutation.yml run when a pair falls below its floor here, when a marked class has no line,
# or when a line names a class no marker does (#909). The point is the property #906 cannot check
# from source: a test that names a class and runs it concurrently, but would pass if it broke.
#
# Format:  <Class simple name> <floor percent> # <what was measured>
#
# Measured on 2026-10-05 (Windows, JDK 21), detected / all mutants. Floors sit 5 to 10 points
# under the measurement, because the dogfood tests are concurrent and their kills vary between
# runs (LicenseGuard measured 59% and 61%). Raise a floor when a test gets stronger; lowering one
# needs the reason in the commit. AsyncTestContext and DetectorRegistry are low by construction:
# most of their mutants sit in per-detector accessors that a ThreadLocal test never reaches.

AsyncTestContext 4 # 31/494 by AsyncTestContextTest
DetectorRegistry 4 # 21/324 by AsyncTestContextTest
ConcurrencyRunner 32 # 95/250 by ConcurrencyRunnerCollisionDogfoodTest
LicenseGuard 52 # 65/106 by LicenseGuardGateOnceDogfoodTest
LicenseValidationCache 32 # 12/28 by LicenseValidationCacheDogfoodTest
RunOutcomes 80 # 21/23 by RunOutcomesTest (2026-10-06)
